---
title: Setup
---

Everything in this clinic runs on the NMFS Openscapes JupyterHub. You do not need an AI account, an API key, or anything installed on your own computer. You need a GitHub account.

## 1. Log in to GitHub

In your browser, log in to [github.com](https://github.com). The hub uses your GitHub account to let you in.

## 2. Go to the hub

Open <https://nmfs-openscapes.2i2c.cloud/> and sign in with GitHub.

## 3. Start a server with 4 GB

On the server options page, choose the **4 GB** size and click **Start**. It can take a minute or two to start.

## 4. Open a terminal

In JupyterLab: **File → New → Terminal**.

## 5. Run the workshop setup script

Choose the tool you are using for the clinic:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Claude Code

In the terminal, run:

```bash
~/shared/workshop/claude-agent-coders
```

When it asks, type the **workshop code** your organizer gives you (or paste the key starting with `sk-` if you were given one). The script gets you a personal key, shows your budget and when it expires, installs Claude Code, and starts it.

The first start asks a few setup questions. Pick a theme. When it asks whether to **trust this folder**, say **no**. It is asking about your home directory, and you do not want the agent working across everything in it. This step is only to get Claude Code installed and your key saved. If Claude Code starts anyway, type `/exit` to close it.

### Antigravity

In the terminal, run the team launcher:

```bash
~/shared/agent-coders/agy-agent-coders
```

The launcher checks for the Antigravity CLI (`agy`), installs it automatically if missing, sets up your terminal `PATH`, adds auto-approved everyday commands to your settings, and configures safety guards.

On your first run, it will walk you through sign-in:

1. Look for the link in the terminal: click **"click to authenticate"** (or copy and paste the URL into your browser).
2. Sign in with your Google account, click through the authorization prompts, and copy the authorization code.
3. Return to the terminal and paste the code.
4. When prompted for your **Google Cloud project code**, paste the project code provided to you (from Jira or your organizer).
5. When prompted, accept the **'Agent Platform'**.

Once authentication completes and you see the agent prompt, type `/exit` to close it so you can complete the repository setup steps below.

:::

## 6. Log in to GitHub from the terminal

```bash
gh auth login
```

Answer the prompts:

- **Where do you use GitHub?** GitHub.com
- **Preferred protocol for Git operations?** HTTPS
- **Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?** Yes
- **How would you like to authenticate?** Login with a web browser

It prints a one-time code. Copy it, open the link it shows, paste the code, and approve. When the terminal says you are logged in, you are done.

## 7. Make your own copy of the practice repository

Create a repository in your own GitHub account from the [NOAA Quarto book template](https://github.com/nmfs-opensci/NOAA-quarto-book), and clone it to the hub:

```bash
cd ~
gh repo create my-quarto-book --template nmfs-opensci/NOAA-quarto-book --public --clone
```

You can use any name in place of `my-quarto-book`. You now have `~/my-quarto-book` on the hub and a matching repository on your GitHub.

## 8. Start your agent in your repository

Open a **new** terminal (the short command names do not work in the terminal you used for setup step 5), navigate to your repository, and start your agent:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Claude Code

```bash
cd ~/my-quarto-book
claude-agent-coders
```

This time, say **yes** to trusting the folder: this is the repository you want the agent to work in.

Try a first prompt:

> What is this repository? List the main files and what they do.

If the agent reads your files and answers, you are set up.

### Antigravity

```bash
cd ~/my-quarto-book
agy-agent-coders
```

::: {.callout-important}
Always start `agy-agent-coders` from inside your project folder (`cd ~/my-quarto-book` first). The folder you start it in is what Antigravity treats as the project boundary, and what the safety guard protects around.
:::

Try a first prompt:

> What is this repository? List the main files and what they do.

If the agent reads your files and answers, you are set up.

**What to expect while working:**

- **Everyday commands run automatically:** `agy-agent-coders` pre-approves everyday tasks—inspecting files (`ls`, `cat`, `grep`, etc.), creating directories (`mkdir`, `touch`), R, Quarto, Python, and read-only git/GitHub actions—so they run without asking. It also automatically accepts edits to files inside your project repository.
- **Unlisted commands ask for approval:** Anything not on the team's auto-approved list (copying, moving, or deleting files, `pip`, or running other software) will prompt for your confirmation before running. This is normal and expected.
- **Safety guards:** The launcher blocks destructive actions like `git reset --hard`, force pushes (`git push --force`), `git clean -f`, and recursive deletions (`rm -r`) outside your project directory. If the agent tries to run one of these, it will be blocked with a message starting with `agent-coders guard:`.

:::

## Good to know

- **Claude Code budget:** `claude-agent-coders --budget` shows what you have spent, your budget, and when your key expires. Spending shows up about a minute after you use Claude.
- **Switch models in Claude Code:** Use `/model`, for example `/model claude-sonnet-4-6`. The default, Claude Haiku 4.5, is the cheapest.
- **Check Antigravity settings:** Run `agy-agent-coders --check` in a terminal to see the auto-approved commands and edit mode configured for your account.
- **Always use the team launcher:** Start Antigravity with `agy-agent-coders`, not plain `agy`. Plain `agy` asks for permission before every single shell command out of the box; `agy-agent-coders` adds everyday commands to your settings and guards against destructive actions.
- **Do not use `agy --sandbox` on the hub:** The hub's container security does not support container sandboxing.
- **Interactive vs non-interactive (`agy -p`):** Non-interactive mode (`agy -p "..."`) stops the whole task at the first command requiring approval, so stick to the interactive terminal session during clinic exercises.
- **Chained commands:** Permission rules match whole words from the start of a command; each segment of a chained command (like `cmd1 && cmd2` or `cmd1 | cmd2`) must match on its own. Chained commands that include unapproved segments will ask for approval.
- **Your personal configurations are preserved:** Both `claude-agent-coders` and `agy-agent-coders` preserve your personal settings and existing configurations.
- **The full paths always work:** If `claude-agent-coders` is not found, use `~/shared/workshop/claude-agent-coders`. If `agy-agent-coders` is not found, use `~/shared/agent-coders/agy-agent-coders`.

## If something goes wrong

### Claude Code issues

- **"That workshop code is not right"**: check the code and try again.
- **"That key was not accepted"**: paste the whole key, starting with `sk-`. If it still fails, ask your organizer.
- **"A key for ... was already issued"**: you, or someone using your name, already signed up. Ask your organizer.
- **"All workshop keys are handed out"**, **"sign-up is closed"** or **"has ended"**: ask your organizer.
- **"not set up yet"** or **"Could not reach the workshop gateway"**: the gateway is not running. Ask your organizer.
- **A key from an earlier workshop**: run `claude-agent-coders --reset`, then `claude-agent-coders` and enter the new code.

### Antigravity issues

- **`agy-agent-coders: command not found`**: Open a new terminal (new terminals load the updated `PATH` with `~/.local/bin`), or run the full path `~/shared/agent-coders/agy-agent-coders`.
- **"agent-coders guard: ..."**: The safety guard prevented a destructive command (such as `git reset --hard` or `rm -r` outside the project folder). This is expected protection; tell the agent to use non-destructive alternatives like `git stash` or a soft reset.
- **Commands asking for confirmation**: Prompts to approve actions like `pip`, `cp`, `mv`, or `rm` are expected behavior for commands not on the everyday whitelist. Review the proposed command and approve it if appropriate.
- **Google Cloud project prompt**: Make sure you paste the exact Google Cloud project code provided in your clinic materials or Jira ticket.
